Style: refined human semi-realistic 3D editorial illustration, natural visible face and realistic adult proportions, approachable ordinary athletic body, believable skin and fabric, not a mannequin, not a plastic toy, not extreme bodybuilding. Graphite sportswear (#2D2D2D), small pastel lime (#E5F88A) and lilac (#B6A1F3) details, plain unbranded trainers. Soft broad studio illumination with subtle contact shadows. Full-body and all equipment completely visible, generous clear margin, uncluttered cutout composition on a fully transparent background. No room scenery, no titles, no text, no arrows, no anatomy overlays, no numbers, no logos or watermarks. Both poses must use exactly the same person, clothing, equipment, camera angle, lighting and scale. No ghosted/interpolated limbs. Clear physical contacts, sensible hands, feet and joints.
REFERENCE USE: Use our own independently generated artwork only for rendering style, material finishes, wardrobe colors and soft lighting. Completely replace its exercise, poses and apparatus as instructed. Use the specific adult described below, with exactly the same face, outfit and equipment in both new poses.
PERSON: An adult man around 30 of East Asian appearance, medium-light skin, short black hair, average natural athletic build, natural calm face, graphite short-sleeved T-shirt and graphite training trousers.
EXERCISE: One wide horizontal diptych, two separate full-body scenes side by side with a large transparent gutter; left preparation, right contracted or lowered position as specified. Equal camera, scale and equipment. Keep every head, hand, foot and equipment part inside the frame. Seated wide-overhand-grip LAT PULLDOWN to the FRONT of the upper chest using the same simple functional cable machine in both scenes. The complete machine has a stable base, a low seat and padded thigh restraint firmly over the thighs, and a high overhead pulley above the midpoint of a single long lat bar. One visible taut cable attaches the CENTER of that bar to the overhead pulley, not the hands. Feet firmly flat on ground, seated knees about 90 degrees, thighs under the pads, upright neutral torso with only a small 10-degree recline. Both hands grip the SAME bar slightly wider than shoulders, palms forward, secure thumbs. Left: bar overhead, arms reaching upward with soft elbows, thighs and feet still secured. Right: elbows draw down toward sides as the bar comes just in FRONT of the upper chest near clavicles, shoulder blades move down/back; same torso angle and same seating position, head not pushed forward. Bar NEVER behind the neck. Do not create duplicate bars/cables, unattached weights or floating seat. Fixed three-quarter FRONT camera, entire athlete and overhead pulley and machine base visible, both scenes equal scale.
